    acceptanceCriteria: Deprovisioning revokes two active sessions and one API key, rejects access token, refresh token, API key, and password login immediately, leaves a same-ID user in another tenant active, emits one redacted USER_DEPROVISIONED event, and a repeated call is a no-op.

  - id: HS-SEC-014
    title: Encryption at rest for secrets
    normativeStatement: HandStack MUST encrypt sensitive values at rest with AES-256-GCM under a 256-bit master key loaded from HANDSTACK_MASTER_KEY, derive purpose keys with HKDF-SHA256, bind ciphertext to organization and plugin context through GCM additional authenticated data, and never include plaintext, key material, or ciphertext in errors or logs.

    owner: security-platform-team
    status: implemented
    risk: critical
    affectedModules:
      - packages/core/src/encryption.ts
      - packages/core/src/index.ts
    publicContracts:

        encryptSecret,
        decryptSecret,
        sealSecret,
        openSecret,
        parseEnvelope,
        EncryptedSecretStore,

  - id: HS-SEC-016
    title: Secure sandbox for untrusted code execution
    normativeStatement: Untrusted plugins, generated code, local tools and MCP stdio commands MUST execute through a SandboxProvider exposing prepare, execute and terminate over a SandboxProfile that enforces CPU, memory, process and execution-time limits, a read-only root filesystem, explicit writable mounts, deny-by-default network with a destination allowlist and SSRF protection, scoped and expiring secret handles, maximum output and log sizes, and tenant and execution identity.

  - id: HS-SEC-017

    normativeStatement: HandStack MUST expose a RFC 7644 SCIM 2.0 endpoint authenticated by a dedicated per-organization bearer token whose full secret is returned only once and stored only as a keyed HMAC digest; the endpoint MUST discover users, groups and service-provider metadata, enforce optimistic concurrency through ETag and If-Match, return RFC 7644 error responses with 401/400/404/409/429 mapping, rate-limit per organization, audit mutations through the durable sink, and derive the organization exclusively from the credential so cross-tenant access is impossible.

  - id: HS-API-014
    title: Typed public TypeScript SDK
    normativeStatement: HandStack MUST provide a dependency-free typed TypeScript SDK that authenticates with an API key held only in memory, sends bearer credentials exclusively in the authorization header, exposes the OpenAI-compatible gateway and the organization-scoped REST surface, supports bounded timeout, cancellation and SSE streaming, and maps RFC 9457 Problem Details into typed actionable errors carrying status, code, requestId, traceId and helpArticleId.
    rationale: Existing OpenAI SDKs and integration code need one stable, typed, transport-safe client without leaking credentials or vendor identifiers, while custom callers benefit from exact route and error contracts.
    owner: platform-team
    status: implemented
    risk: high
    affectedModules:
      - packages/sdk/src/index.ts

      - packages/sdk/src/sse.ts
    publicContracts: [HandStack, HandStackApiError, HandStackSdkError, FetchLike, parseSse]
    dataEntities: []
    securityPrivacyImpact: API keys are never persisted or written to URLs or request bodies and are sent only in the authorization header; timeouts and cancellation use AbortSignal; typed errors expose only closed Problem Details fields and never internal stacks; SSE parsing bounds memory and stops at the [DONE] sentinel.

    title: Scoped multi-metric rate limiting
    normativeStatement: HandStack MUST enforce rate limits across organization, group, user, API key, agent, model and capability scopes using requests-per-minute, tokens-per-minute, concurrent-requests and daily-requests metrics, keep every counter tenant-scoped so one organization's limit never consumes another's capacity, and return a typed 429 with retry guidance.
    rationale: Shared AI capacity requires per-tenant and per-principal admission control to prevent one consumer from starving others while preserving deterministic denial behavior across compact and distributed profiles.
    owner: platform-team
    status: implemented
    risk: high
    affectedModules:
      - packages/rate-limiting/src/index.ts
      - packages/rate-limiting/package.json
    publicContracts:
      [
        ScopedRateLimiter,
        RateLimitStore,
        InMemoryRateLimitStore,
        RateLimitRule,
        RateLimitContext,
        RateLimitDecision,
        raiseRateLimitError,
      ]
    dataEntities: [RateLimitRule, RateLimitDecision]
    securityPrivacyImpact: Every counter key embeds organizationId plus scope and scopeId so tenants cannot bleed capacity; concurrency slots are acquired and released explicitly; denials use the shared typed RateLimitError and expose only the exceeded scope, metric and retry seconds.

    testPaths: [packages/rate-limiting/tests/rate-limit.test.ts]
    documentationArticleIds: [getting-started/rate-limiting]
    introducedVersion: 0.37.0

# Register and evaluate models

## Purpose and expected outcome

Create tenant-scoped provider and model definitions without coupling product rules to vendor model names, then promote a model only after a versioned evaluation gate passes.

## Prerequisites

- An initialized canonical database adapter.
- A provider secret stored behind a `SecretProvider` reference when credentials are required.
- A versioned evaluation suite and approved dataset.

## Steps

1. Register a `ProviderDefinition` with its adapter, allowed data classifications, and optional secret reference.
2. Register a `ModelDefinition` in `DRAFT` with the vendor model ID, aliases, capabilities, context window, and normalized USD pricing.
3. Register an approved, versioned dataset with classification, provenance, owner, and retention. Production-derived cases also require an explicit legal basis and sanitization.
4. Register and run the affected suite through `CoreEvaluationProvider`. Every model gate includes the product minimum quality, schema/tool correctness, safety/prompt-injection/leakage, latency, token, and cost criteria.
5. Record the versioned gate using the returned run result. The registry asks the provider to reload and validate the persisted run, suite, and dataset; caller-supplied booleans cannot satisfy the gate. A failed gate leaves the model in `DRAFT`; a passing gate moves it to `EVALUATED`.
6. Approve the evaluated model, then publish it. Publication revalidates that the referenced gate exists, passed, and matches the recorded suite version.

Application execution must go through `ModelExecutionRuntime` with the organization ID, an internal model ID or alias, and the request data classification. The runtime resolves the published definition and enabled provider in that organization, verifies the provider classification allowlist, creates the registered adapter, and only then maps to `providerModel`. A secret resolver receives the organization and the provider's stored reference; callers never supply vendor model IDs or secret values.

Use `createOfficialProviderFactories` to wire the initial provider set. Public provider-specific values belong in `ProviderDefinition.configuration`: `resourceName` and `apiVersion` for Azure OpenAI, `region` for Bedrock, and optional `applicationUrl`/`applicationName` for OpenRouter. Custom compatible URLs remain in `baseUrl`. Bedrock must use workload identity or the AWS credential chain and rejects a stored secret reference. Factory construction does not resolve credentials; the adapter invokes the tenant-scoped resolver only when it sends a request.

For OpenAI-compatible APIs, use `OpenAICompatibleProvider` or the `createOpenAIProvider` wrapper. Use `createOllamaProvider` for the loopback Ollama endpoint. Remote endpoints require HTTPS; plain HTTP is accepted only for an explicitly enabled loopback host. API keys are resolved at request time and never enter request bodies, registry records, or diagnostic errors.

For native APIs, use `createAnthropicProvider` or `createGeminiProvider`. Both adapters translate the neutral message, system instruction, tool, streaming, finish-reason, and usage contracts into the vendor envelope. Their async key resolvers run for every request; Anthropic uses `x-api-key` and Gemini uses `x-goog-api-key`, so credentials never appear in URLs or payloads.

Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, and vLLM use `createAzureOpenAIProvider`, `createOpenRouterProvider`, and `createVllmProvider`. Azure requires an explicit resource, deployment, and API version and sends its key only in `api-key`; its known deployment is the model catalog. OpenRouter accepts optional public application attribution headers. vLLM permits plain HTTP only at an explicit loopback URL.

AWS Bedrock uses `createBedrockProvider` with an explicit region. Its default transport delegates request signing, session tokens, and temporary-credential refresh to the official AWS SDK credential provider chain, then translates the model catalog and Converse/ConverseStream envelopes into the same neutral contract. Never persist AWS credentials in the model registry; configure the workload identity or approved AWS credential provider externally.

## Administrative API

Grant `models.manage` to the administrative principal, obtain a short-lived bearer access token, and use these versioned endpoints:

- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/providers`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompts`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompts/{promptId}/versions`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-datasets`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-suites`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-runs`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/evaluation-gates`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/approve`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/publish`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/evaluation-gates`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/approve`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/publish`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/model-responses`
- `GET /api/openapi.json`

The organization in the route must exactly match the access token organization. Provider creation accepts `secretReference` as write-only input; responses expose only `hasSecret`. Put only public transport configuration in `configuration`. Keys resembling passwords, tokens, credentials, API keys, or secrets are rejected, and reads defensively redact them. Unknown request fields are rejected. New models always start in `DRAFT` and refer to an enabled provider in the same organization.

Dataset responses expose governance metadata and `caseCount`, but never case inputs, expected outputs, or legal-basis text. Registration requires approval, provenance, ownership, retention, classification, and at least one uniquely identified case. Production-derived datasets additionally require both sanitization and an explicit legal basis. Suites bind an exact dataset ID/version and must include every product-minimum model metric with finite, non-duplicated thresholds. Evaluation execution and lifecycle transitions are separate operations; clients never submit run scores.

Each executable case uses `input.messages` in the neutral chat format and may include neutral `input.tools` and an explicit `input.dataClassification` (otherwise the dataset classification applies). Declarative expectations may contain exact `content`, `contentIncludes`, `contentExcludes`, `jsonObject`, and ordered `toolCalls` with optional arguments. The official evaluation runner resolves the draft model and enabled provider inside the same organization, enforces the provider classification allowlist, executes the official adapter, and derives task/schema/tool/safety/injection/leakage, latency, token, and USD-cost scores from the actual response. It stores only evidence digests. Metrics that require a scorer not present in the official runner fail closed rather than receiving an invented score.

Create a run with only `modelDefinitionId`, `suiteId`, and `suiteVersion`. Record its gate with only the returned 64-character `runId`; the server reloads the run and reconstructs the gate, so request bodies containing scores are rejected. Approval requires a passing persisted gate, and publication requires that gate to remain present, passing, and current. Model credential references supported by the API runtime use `env://HANDSTACK_SECRET_<NAME>`; resolution is lazy and values never enter registry, evaluation records, API responses, or errors.

Grant `models.execute` separately to application callers. Send an internal model alias, data classification, neutral `messages`, and optional neutral `tools` to `model-responses`; callers never send a provider adapter, vendor model ID, endpoint, or credential. The route resolves only a published model in the token organization and returns the common `ChatResponse` envelope. The same route is contract-tested after real evaluation promotion through OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Gemini adapters. Draft models, disallowed classifications, cross-tenant access, and missing execution permission fail closed.

Prompt administration requires `prompts.manage`. A `Prompt` owns a stable slug, while every `PromptVersion` is an immutable snapshot of content, declared variables, content digest, and internal model route. Placeholders use `{{variable}}` and must exactly match their declarations. Run the normal evaluation endpoint with `promptVersionId`; the server binds its digest and rejects a mismatched model route. Record, approve, and publish that exact version through the prompt-version lifecycle endpoints. New content or a new model route starts another `DRAFT` version and cannot inherit or reuse the earlier run or gate.

## Verify

Resolve the model by ID and by alias and confirm it is visible only in its organization. Attempting to record a fabricated run, omit a minimum metric, approve, or publish before a passing persisted gate must fail.

Call `model-responses` with the same neutral request and three published aliases backed by OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Gemini. Confirm all three return the common response shape, while the same call against a draft alias fails before any provider request.

Also fetch `/api/openapi.json`, confirm the versioned collections and lifecycle operations are present, and verify that an unprivileged or cross-organization token receives `403` without returning provider or evaluation data. Confirm that approval before evaluation, a request-supplied score map, and a nonexistent run digest all fail.

## Troubleshooting

- Alias collision means another model in the organization already owns that alias.
- “Enabled provider not found” means the referenced provider is absent, disabled, or belongs to another organization.
- A stale-gate failure requires rerunning the current suite version.
- An `audit unavailable` failure means the administrative mutation was rolled back because its mandatory audit event could not be persisted; restore the database/audit path before retrying.
- `MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `MODEL_NOT_PUBLISHED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `CLASSIFICATION_DENIED`, or `ADAPTER_NOT_REGISTERED` means execution was blocked locally before provider traffic. `PROVIDER_FAILURE` deliberately hides the upstream failure.
- `ProviderRequestError` exposes only `TIMEOUT`, `CANCELLED`, `NETWORK`, `HTTP`, or `INVALID_RESPONSE` and an optional status. Inspect the provider privately because upstream bodies are deliberately discarded.
- Native adapter errors expose the same closed code set through `AnthropicProviderError` or `GeminiProviderError`; neither error retains upstream bodies, URLs, headers, or network messages.

## Security, budget, and audit implications

Registry records contain secret references, never secret values. Data classification is explicit at the provider boundary. The OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint follows the same published-model and virtual-key checks as chat, and reserves then settles budget from the provider-reported prompt-token usage. Providers that do not advertise embeddings fail closed. Evaluation execution may consume provider budget and must report usage through the common budget pipeline.

Provider and model registration, dataset and suite registration, evaluation completion, gate recording, approval, and publication append a tenant-scoped audit event in the same database. Administrative mutations and audit persistence are atomic: if the mandatory event cannot be stored, the mutation is rolled back. Evaluation reruns reuse the deterministic run and do not duplicate its event.

Audit metadata contains only approved scalar provenance such as internal resource IDs, suite and dataset versions, lifecycle transitions, classification, outcome, and counts. It never includes prompts, dataset cases, scores, evidence, provider responses, vendor model IDs, secret references, or credential values. `AiGovernanceOpenTelemetry` emits spans, an operation counter, and a duration histogram using only closed operation/outcome attributes for registry, evaluation, chat, and streaming execution.

## Rollback

Deprecate the affected model and restore the last approved definition and gate combination. Never rewrite historical gate results.

## Prerequisites

- Um adapter de banco canônico inicializado.
- Secret do provider armazenado por referência de `SecretProvider` quando credenciais forem necessárias.
- Uma evaluation suite versionada e dataset aprovado.

## Steps

1. Registre um `ProviderDefinition` com adapter, classificações de dados permitidas e referência opcional de secret.
2. Registre um `ModelDefinition` em `DRAFT` com ID do vendor, aliases, capabilities, context window e pricing normalizado em USD.
3. Registre um dataset aprovado e versionado com classificação, proveniência, owner e retenção. Casos derivados de produção também exigem base legal explícita e sanitização.
4. Registre e execute a suite afetada por `CoreEvaluationProvider`. Todo gate de modelo inclui os critérios mínimos de produto para qualidade, schema/tools, segurança contra prompt injection/vazamento, latência, tokens e custo.
5. Registre o gate versionado usando o resultado retornado. O registry pede ao provider que releia e valide run, suite e dataset persistidos; booleanos fornecidos pelo caller não satisfazem o gate. Um gate falho mantém o modelo em `DRAFT`; um gate aprovado move-o para `EVALUATED`.
6. Aprove o modelo avaliado e publique-o. A publicação revalida que o gate referenciado existe, passou e corresponde à versão registrada da suite.

A execução da aplicação deve passar por `ModelExecutionRuntime` com Organization ID, ID interno ou alias do modelo e classificação dos dados do request. O runtime resolve a definição publicada e o provider habilitado naquela organização, verifica a allowlist de classificação, cria o adapter registrado e somente então mapeia para `providerModel`. O secret resolver recebe a organização e a referência persistida do provider; callers nunca fornecem IDs de modelo externos ou valores de secret.

Use `createOfficialProviderFactories` para conectar o conjunto inicial de providers. Valores públicos específicos ficam em `ProviderDefinition.configuration`: `resourceName` e `apiVersion` para Azure OpenAI, `region` para Bedrock e `applicationUrl`/`applicationName` opcionais para OpenRouter. URLs compatíveis customizadas permanecem em `baseUrl`. Bedrock deve usar workload identity ou credential chain AWS e rejeita secret reference persistida. A construção da factory não resolve credenciais; o adapter chama o resolver tenant-scoped somente quando envia um request.

Para APIs OpenAI-compatible, use `OpenAICompatibleProvider` ou o wrapper `createOpenAIProvider`. Use `createOllamaProvider` para o endpoint loopback do Ollama. Endpoints remotos exigem HTTPS; HTTP simples é aceito somente para host loopback explicitamente habilitado. API keys são resolvidas a cada request e nunca entram no body, registry ou erros de diagnóstico.

Para APIs nativas, use `createAnthropicProvider` ou `createGeminiProvider`. Ambos traduzem os contratos neutros de mensagens, instrução de sistema, tools, streaming, finish reason e usage para o envelope do vendor. Os resolvers assíncronos de chave executam em cada request; Anthropic usa `x-api-key` e Gemini usa `x-goog-api-key`, portanto credenciais nunca aparecem em URLs ou payloads.

Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter e vLLM usam `createAzureOpenAIProvider`, `createOpenRouterProvider` e `createVllmProvider`. Azure exige resource, deployment e versão de API explícitos e envia a chave somente em `api-key`; o deployment conhecido forma seu catálogo de modelos. OpenRouter aceita headers públicos opcionais de atribuição da aplicação. vLLM permite HTTP simples somente em URL loopback explícita.

AWS Bedrock usa `createBedrockProvider` com região explícita. Seu transporte padrão delega assinatura, session tokens e renovação de credenciais temporárias à credential provider chain do SDK oficial AWS, traduzindo depois o catálogo e os envelopes Converse/ConverseStream para o mesmo contrato neutro. Nunca persista credenciais AWS no model registry; configure workload identity ou um credential provider AWS aprovado externamente.

## API administrativa

Conceda `models.manage` ao principal administrativo, obtenha um bearer access token de curta duração e use estes endpoints versionados:

- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/providers`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompts`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompts/{promptId}/versions`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-datasets`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-suites`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/evaluation-runs`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/evaluation-gates`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/approve`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/models/{modelId}/publish`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/evaluation-gates`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/approve`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/prompt-versions/{promptVersionId}/publish`
- `POST /api/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/model-responses`
- `GET /api/openapi.json`

A organização da rota deve coincidir exatamente com a organização do access token. A criação do provider aceita `secretReference` somente como entrada de escrita; respostas expõem apenas `hasSecret`. Coloque em `configuration` somente configuração pública de transporte. Chaves semelhantes a passwords, tokens, credentials, API keys ou secrets são rejeitadas, e leituras também as removem defensivamente. Campos desconhecidos são rejeitados. Novos modelos sempre começam em `DRAFT` e apontam para provider habilitado da mesma organização.

Respostas de dataset expõem metadata de governança e `caseCount`, mas nunca inputs, resultados esperados ou o texto da base legal dos casos. O registro exige aprovação, proveniência, owner, retenção, classificação e pelo menos um caso com ID único. Datasets derivados de produção exigem também sanitização e base legal explícitas. Suites vinculam ID e versão exatos do dataset e devem incluir todas as métricas mínimas de modelo do produto com thresholds finitos e não duplicados. Execução da avaliação e transições de lifecycle são operações separadas; clientes nunca enviam scores de runs.

Cada caso executável usa `input.messages` no formato neutro de chat e pode incluir `input.tools` neutras e `input.dataClassification` explícita (caso contrário, vale a classificação do dataset). Expectativas declarativas podem conter `content` exato, `contentIncludes`, `contentExcludes`, `jsonObject` e `toolCalls` ordenadas com arguments opcionais. O runner oficial resolve o modelo draft e o provider habilitado dentro da mesma organização, aplica a allowlist de classificação do provider, executa o adapter oficial e deriva scores de task/schema/tools/segurança/injection/vazamento, latência, tokens e custo em USD da resposta real. Somente digests de evidência são persistidos. Métricas que exigem scorer ausente no runner oficial falham de forma fechada, sem nota inventada.

Crie um run somente com `modelDefinitionId`, `suiteId` e `suiteVersion`. Registre o gate somente com o `runId` de 64 caracteres retornado; o servidor relê o run e reconstrói o gate, portanto bodies contendo scores são rejeitados. Aprovação exige gate persistido aprovado, e publicação exige que esse gate continue presente, aprovado e atual. Referências de credencial de modelo suportadas pelo runtime da API usam `env://HANDSTACK_SECRET_<NAME>`; a resolução é lazy e os valores nunca entram no registry, registros de evaluation, respostas ou erros.

Conceda `models.execute` separadamente aos callers da aplicação. Envie alias interno do modelo, classificação de dados, `messages` neutras e `tools` neutras opcionais para `model-responses`; callers nunca enviam adapter, ID externo do modelo, endpoint ou credencial. A rota resolve somente modelo publicado na organização do token e retorna o envelope comum `ChatResponse`. A mesma rota é testada após promoção por avaliação real através dos adapters OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic e Gemini. Modelos draft, classificações não permitidas, acesso cross-tenant e falta da permissão de execução falham de forma fechada.

A administração de prompts exige `prompts.manage`. Um `Prompt` possui slug estável, enquanto cada `PromptVersion` é um snapshot imutável de conteúdo, variáveis declaradas, digest e model route interno. Placeholders usam `{{variable}}` e devem corresponder exatamente às declarações. Execute o endpoint normal de avaliação com `promptVersionId`; o servidor vincula seu digest e rejeita model route divergente. Registre, aprove e publique aquela versão exata pelos endpoints de lifecycle. Conteúdo ou model route novo começa em outra versão `DRAFT`, sem herdar ou reutilizar o run ou gate anterior.

## Verify

Resolva o modelo por ID e alias e confirme que ele aparece somente em sua organização. Tentativas de registrar run fabricado, omitir métrica mínima, aprovar ou publicar sem gate persistido aprovado devem falhar.

Chame `model-responses` com o mesmo request neutro e três aliases publicados associados a OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic e Gemini. Confirme que os três retornam o formato comum e que a chamada contra um alias draft falha antes de qualquer request ao provider.

Consulte também `/api/openapi.json`, confirme as collections versionadas e operações de lifecycle e verifique que token sem permissão ou de outra organização recebe `403` sem retornar dados de provider ou evaluation. Confirme também que aprovação antes da avaliação, score map fornecido no request e digest de run inexistente falham.

## Troubleshooting

- Colisão de alias indica que outro modelo da organização já possui esse alias.
- “Enabled provider not found” indica provider ausente, desabilitado ou pertencente a outra organização.
- Falha de gate obsoleto exige nova execução da versão atual da suite.
- Falha `audit unavailable` indica que a mutação administrativa sofreu rollback porque o evento obrigatório não pôde ser persistido; restaure o caminho de banco/auditoria antes de tentar novamente.
- `MODEL_NOT_FOUND`, `MODEL_NOT_PUBLISHED`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `CLASSIFICATION_DENIED` ou `ADAPTER_NOT_REGISTERED` indica bloqueio local antes de tráfego ao provider. `PROVIDER_FAILURE` oculta deliberadamente a falha upstream.
- `ProviderRequestError` expõe apenas `TIMEOUT`, `CANCELLED`, `NETWORK`, `HTTP` ou `INVALID_RESPONSE` e status opcional. Inspecione o provider de forma privada porque bodies upstream são descartados deliberadamente.
- Erros dos adapters nativos expõem o mesmo conjunto fechado por `AnthropicProviderError` ou `GeminiProviderError`; nenhum deles retém body upstream, URL, headers ou mensagens de rede.

## Security, budget, and audit implications

O registry contém referências de secret, nunca seus valores. A classificação de dados é explícita no boundary do provider. O endpoint OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` aplica as mesmas verificações de modelo publicado e virtual key do chat, reservando e liquidando o budget com base nos tokens de prompt reportados pelo provider. Providers sem capability de embeddings falham de forma fechada. Avaliações podem consumir budget e devem reportar esse uso pelo pipeline comum.

Registro de provider e modelo, registro de dataset e suite, conclusão da avaliação, registro de gate, aprovação e publicação adicionam um audit event tenant-aware no mesmo banco. A mutação administrativa e a persistência de auditoria são atômicas: se o evento obrigatório não puder ser gravado, a mutação sofre rollback. Reruns reutilizam o run determinístico e não duplicam seu evento.

O metadata de auditoria contém somente proveniência escalar aprovada, como IDs internos, versões de suite/dataset, transições de lifecycle, classificação, outcome e contagens. Nunca contém prompts, casos do dataset, scores, evidências, respostas do provider, IDs externos de modelo, referências de secret ou credenciais. `AiGovernanceOpenTelemetry` emite spans, contador de operações e histograma de duração usando apenas atributos fechados de operação/outcome para registry, evaluation, chat e streaming.

## Rollback

Deprecie o modelo afetado e restaure a última combinação aprovada de definição e gate. Nunca reescreva resultados históricos de gates.

## Related articles

- [Autenticação e sessões](/help/getting-started/authentication-sessions)
